season.evidence: Web: Washington hike reports and guidebook pages describe snow lingering into early July and the best window as late summer into fall; peak ascents peak in Oct (larches) with spring ski ascents Apr-Jun. Stored Jun-Oct kept.

facts.text: In late July the basin below the final slope is snow-free, and a direct line over slabs and boulders just left of the sloping bench reaches the last low point of the summit ridge in about twenty minutes.
Mountain goats are common in the upper basin in late July, so give them room.
Dogs are not permitted in Headlight Basin or at Ingalls Pass; parties with a dog use the Lake Ann route instead.

season.evidence: Web: May reports describe a snow-covered, steep descent toward the pass above Lake Ann, July reports find snow on the route, and guidebook pages favor late summer to early fall; larch season in October draws many climbers. Stored Jun-Oct kept.

track.why: Logged Fortune Creek Pass, the trail name the Lake Ann route goes by; the line leaves the Esmeralda Basin Trail westward, climbs to the saddle above Lake Ann and follows the west ridge to the summit (matches our text and a Sept 2021 report describing exactly that path). Summited, round trip 15 m from our trailhead pin, 28 Aug 2023. Note it also continues to South Ingalls and returns by Ingalls Pass.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Headlight Basin / Ingalls Peak loop, not the Lake Ann line.

facts.text: By late September the tarn near Lake Ann and the lake itself can be almost dry, so carry the water you need.

notes: Several summit tracks climb Ingalls Peak first; they were not assigned. The east-slope route has no unambiguous recorded track.
